classification.difficultyReason: Discover how pouch sizes extend an uninterrupted range of subset sums, then adapt that construction to five pouches totalling twenty-three and justify every payment amount.

content.prompt: To protect his money from pickpockets, a merchant keeps his coins in several pouches so that he can pay any amount without revealing how much money he has, just by handing over the correct pouches. On the first day of trading he has six coins, so he places one coin in the first pouch, two coins in the second, and three coins in the third. This allows him to pay any value from one to six coins without having to open a pouch. The next day of trading he has 23 coins and five pouches. How should he distribute the coins to ensure that he can pay any amount from 1 to 23 coins?

inlines.text: Combine the first three pouches to make 0–7 coins, then add one or both 8-coin pouches.

answer.worked:
Put 1, 2, 4, 8 and 8 coins in the five pouches.

$1+2+4+8+8=23$.

The 1-, 2- and 4-coin pouches make every amount from 0 to 7: $0,1,2,1+2,4,4+1,4+2,4+2+1$.

Adding one 8-coin pouch gives every amount from 8 to 15. Adding both 8-coin pouches gives every amount from 16 to 23. Thus every payment from 1 to 23 coins is possible without opening a pouch.
